title: String Quartet No. 14 in C-sharp minor
hook: Seven movements played without a break; Beethoven thought it the best of his quartets.

painting.title: Self-Portrait with Two Circles
painting.pairingNote: A painter in his last years, working broadly and freely, in front of two circles no one has ever explained; Beethoven’s late quartet is just as personal, and writers still argue over how to read it.

facts: Beethoven wrote it between the end of 1825 and the summer of 1826, aged fifty-five and deaf. It was the last of three quartets written one after another, Op. 132, Op. 130 and this one. According to his friend the violinist Karl Holz, Beethoven later called it the greatest of his quartets.
It has seven movements, played without a break. When Holz asked whether the players could stop to tune, Beethoven allowed only a short pause after the fifth movement.

On the copy he sent to his publisher, Schott, Beethoven wrote as a joke that the quartet was “put together from pilferings of this and that”. When the worried publisher asked, he replied that it was in fact brand new.

He dedicated it to Baron Joseph von Stutterheim, the officer who took his nephew Karl into the army after Karl’s attempted suicide in the summer of 1826. Beethoven never heard it played: it was printed after his death in 1827. Holz later recalled that in November 1828, days before his own death, Franz Schubert asked to hear it.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a slow fugue (I), a light dance (II), a short bridge (III), a theme with variations (IV), a quick scherzo (V), a brief lament (VI), a fierce finale (VII).

movements.heading: Adagio ma non troppo e molto espressivo
movements.tempo: Adagio ma non troppo e molto espressivo
movements.summary: The quartet begins with a slow, quiet [[fugue|fugue]]: one sad tune, played first by a single violin, then taken up by each instrument in turn and woven against itself. Richard Wagner called it the most melancholy music ever written. It stays soft almost to the end.

mainIdeas.name: The fugue tune
mainIdeas.description: four long notes that rise, then fall, with a held, aching third note. The same four-note shape runs through Beethoven’s other late quartets.

mainIdeas.name: The texture
mainIdeas.description: four lines moving slowly over one another, as in old church music.

stops.hear: The first violin alone, very slow and quiet: a few long notes that rise and sink
stops.happening: The fugue tune, in C-sharp minor

stops.hear: The same tune enters in the second violin, then the viola, then the cello; the lines pile up
stops.happening: The four voices of the fugue enter one by one

stops.hear: After a long quiet stretch, the first loud passage, all four together
stops.happening: The fugue reaches a far-off key and swells for a moment

stops.hear: Very low in the cello, the tune in long, stretched notes
stops.happening: The fugue tune in slow motion, called augmentation

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Soft again; the music comes to rest on one bare note, C-sharp, played in octaves
stops.happening: The bare note leads into the next movement, a half step higher

notice: Follow one instrument, for example the cello, and listen to how long it waits before it plays the tune.
The last note is a bare C-sharp. The next movement begins one step up, on D, as if the music has simply lifted.

movements.heading: Allegro molto vivace
movements.summary: A light, quick dance in D major, in a lilting six-beat rhythm, after the stillness of the fugue. It is built almost entirely from one folk-like tune, which keeps returning between sudden loud outbursts.

mainIdeas.name: The tune
mainIdeas.description: a simple, rocking melody in the first violin, very soft at first.

mainIdeas.name: The outbursts
mainIdeas.description: short, loud chords that break in and are gone again.

stops.hear: Very soft and light: a rocking tune in the first violin, in a skipping rhythm
stops.happening: The dance tune, in D major

stops.hear: Sudden loud chords, then soft again
The tune comes back, passed between the instruments
Loud, then very loud; then a quick fade
stops.happening: The last outbursts and a soft ending

notice: Compare the mood with the fugue. The key has moved only one note higher, but the music sounds like a different world.

movements.heading: Allegro moderato – Adagio
movements.summary: Not much more than half a minute long: two loud chords, a few bars of free, speaking music in the first violin, and a slow cadence that opens the door to the next movement.

mainIdeas.description: Two firm chords, like a call to attention.

mainIdeas.name: The violin’s phrases
mainIdeas.description: free in rhythm, like a singer’s [[recitative|recitative]].

stops.hear: Two loud chords, all four together
The first violin alone, quick then slow, like someone speaking; the others answer softly
stops.happening: A short recitative, leading to the Adagio

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: A soft, unfinished chord
stops.happening: It leads straight into the variations

notice: Listen to how short this is. Beethoven gave it a number of its own, but it works as a bridge.

movements.heading: Andante ma non troppo e molto cantabile
movements.tempo: Andante ma non troppo e molto cantabile
movements.summary: The heart of the quartet and its longest movement: a gentle tune in A major, followed by six [[variation|variation]]s and a long [[coda|coda]]. Each variation keeps the outline of the tune but changes its speed, rhythm and mood.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: a simple, singing tune in short steps, shared between the two violins, which answer each other phrase by phrase.

mainIdeas.name: The variations
mainIdeas.description: a march, a playful duet, a slow and rocking one, a light one, a hymn.

stops.hear: A simple, gentle tune; the two violins take turns with its short phrases
The tune is decorated: the lower instruments trade fragments of it in a jumpy, dotted rhythm
A little faster, in four firm beats, almost a march
Lighter and teasing: two instruments imitate each other, one a beat behind the other
Slower, in a rocking rhythm; the four lines are closely woven
Quick and light; the tune is reduced to its outline
Very slow and soft, like a hymn; the cello keeps interrupting with a short trembling figure
stops.happening: Variation 6 (Adagio, in nine beats to the bar)

stops.hear: Quicker; each instrument plays a short, flowing solo in turn, and a new variation seems to begin and is broken off

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The last bars of the tune, softly repeated

notice: Try to hum the tune at the start. Then listen for how much of it you can still find in each variation. In some it is clear, in others only its shape remains.
In variation 6, listen to the cello. Its little shudders disturb the calm of the hymn.

movements.heading: Presto
movements.summary: A fast, bright [[scherzo|scherzo]] in E major, almost childlike in its tune. The cello starts it with a short call followed by silence. Its quieter middle part comes round twice, and near the end all four players bow close to the bridge, which makes a glassy, whispering sound.

mainIdeas.name: The call
mainIdeas.description: a few quick notes in the cello, then a full stop.

mainIdeas.name: The scherzo tune
mainIdeas.description: a quick, simple melody like a nursery rhyme, tossed between the instruments.

mainIdeas.name: The middle part
mainIdeas.description: smoother and more singing, in A major.

stops.hear: A short call from the cello, a silence, then a quick, simple tune
Smoother and more singing; a new tune in long phrases
The quick tune again
The smooth tune once more
The quick tune, for the last time
Very quiet, a thin, glassy, whispering sound from all four
stops.happening: [[sul-ponticello|sul ponticello]]: bowing right next to the bridge

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: A few loud, sharp chords

notice: Listen for the whispering sound near ≈ 4:45. It is the same tune, played with the bow almost on the bridge.

movements.heading: Adagio quasi un poco andante
movements.summary: A short, sad song in G-sharp minor, two minutes long. The viola begins alone; the others join with a slow, quiet melody. It does not end: it stops on a chord that leads straight into the finale.

mainIdeas.name: The viola’s opening
mainIdeas.description: a slow, dark phrase that turns the first notes of the opening fugue upside down.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: a quiet lament in the upper instruments.

stops.hear: The viola alone, slow and low
The others join; a slow, sorrowful melody in the violins

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The music stops on an unresolved chord
stops.happening: It leads straight into the finale

notice: Listen to the very first notes of the viola and think back to the fugue that opened the quartet. Beethoven has turned its first notes upside down.

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: A fierce, driving finale back in C-sharp minor, the only movement of the seven in [[sonata-form|sonata form]]. It is full of hard, galloping rhythms, but a soaring, lyrical theme brings moments of relief. It ends with three loud chords in C-sharp major.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: loud, hard notes in octaves with a jagged, galloping rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: The line in long notes
mainIdeas.description: over a galloping repeated note, the first violin sings a line whose shape recalls the fugue of the first movement.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a soaring, lyrical tune in the first violin.

stops.hear: Loud and hard: all four in octaves, in a jagged, galloping rhythm
Quieter; a galloping repeated note in the viola, and a long-note line above it
stops.happening: The fugue’s shape returns in the finale

stops.hear: Softer and singing: a long, soaring tune in the first violin
Loud again; the galloping rhythm is thrown from instrument to instrument
The hard opening theme, very loud
The soaring tune once more
Very quiet, then building again

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: Three loud chords

notice: Listen for the long-note line near ≈ 0:20. It is the shape of the opening fugue, now inside the fastest music of the quartet.
The very end turns from minor to major, but the last chords sound hard won, not happy.

threads.title: No breaks
threads.body: The seven movements follow one another without stopping. Three of them (III, VI, and in a way II) are short links. The big ones are the fugue, the variations, the scherzo and the finale.

threads.title: One shape
threads.body: The fugue tune at the start comes back: turned upside down by the viola in VI, and inside the fast music of VII.

threads.title: Four voices
threads.body: In the fugue they are equals. In the variations the violins share the tune; in the scherzo the cello sets everything off.

threads.title: Keys that climb
threads.body: C-sharp minor, then D major one step up, then a journey through other keys before the finale returns home.
